quests.hint: Recognising the clear difference between two similar-seeming things.
quests.explanation: 'Distinguish between' two things is the everyday way to say it. It's a more formal way of saying 'tell apart.'
quests.textToSpeak: It is important to ___ between correlation and causation when analysing data.
quests.correctAnswer: It is important to distinguish between correlation and causation when analysing data.

quests.hint: Pulling ideas from several different sources together into one coherent whole.
quests.explanation: Synthesise takes an 's' in British English ('synthesize' in American English). The noun form is 'synthesis.'
quests.textToSpeak: The essay asks you to ___ multiple sources and draw your own overall conclusion.
quests.correctAnswer: The essay asks you to synthesise multiple sources and draw your own overall conclusion.

quests.hint: Expressing something as an exact number or amount.
quests.explanation: 'Difficult to quantify' is a common phrase for things that are real but hard to measure, like emotions. The noun form is 'quantity.'
quests.textToSpeak: It is very difficult to ___ the emotional benefits of a strong community support network.
quests.correctAnswer: It is very difficult to quantify the emotional benefits of a strong community support network.

quests.hint: Giving good reasons that explain and defend a decision.
quests.explanation: 'Justify a decision' is the go-to phrase. The noun form is 'justification' — 'a valid justification.'
quests.textToSpeak: She was asked to ___ her decision to restructure the department at such short notice.
quests.correctAnswer: She was asked to justify her decision to restructure the department at such short notice.

quests.hint: Admitting, often reluctantly, that a point someone else made is actually valid.
quests.explanation: 'Concede that' is followed by a full clause. It's a more gracious way of saying 'admit' during a disagreement.
quests.textToSpeak: In the debate, she was willing to ___ that the opposing argument had some merit.
quests.correctAnswer: In the debate, she was willing to concede that the opposing argument had some merit.

quests.hint: Saying or showing the exact opposite of what was previously claimed.
quests.explanation: 'Contradict the conclusions' or 'contradict yourself' both work. The noun form is 'contradiction.'
quests.textToSpeak: The new evidence seemed to ___ the conclusions of every study that came before it.
quests.correctAnswer: The new evidence seemed to contradict the conclusions of every study that came before it.

quests.hint: Widespread and very common in a particular group or place.
quests.explanation: 'Remarkably prevalent among' is a common phrase in social research. The noun form is 'prevalence.'
quests.textToSpeak: Smartphone addiction has become remarkably ___ among young people in recent years.
quests.correctAnswer: Smartphone addiction has become remarkably prevalent among young people in recent years.

quests.hint: Highly advanced and complex, often in a clever or refined way.
quests.explanation: 'A sophisticated algorithm' or 'sophisticated technology' are the everyday way to say it. It's the opposite of 'basic' or 'simplistic.'
quests.textToSpeak: The new software uses a highly ___ algorithm to predict user behaviour and preferences.
quests.correctAnswer: The new software uses a highly sophisticated algorithm to predict user behaviour and preferences.

quests.hint: Adding more detail to explain a point more fully.
quests.explanation: 'Elaborate on' a point is the one that sounds most natural. As an adjective (pronounced differently), elaborate also means highly detailed.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you ___ on that last point? I did not quite follow your reasoning there.
quests.correctAnswer: Could you elaborate on that last point? I did not quite follow your reasoning there.

quests.hint: Making something stronger by adding extra support.
quests.explanation: 'Reinforce confidence' or 'reinforce an idea' both work. It literally means adding strength, like reinforcing a wall.
quests.textToSpeak: Practising speaking every day will ___ your confidence and fluency over time.
quests.correctAnswer: Practising speaking every day will reinforce your confidence and fluency over time.

quests.hint: Understood without being directly stated in words.
quests.explanation: 'An implicit agreement' is one everyone understands without discussing it aloud. Its opposite is 'explicit,' stated clearly and directly.
quests.textToSpeak: There was an ___ agreement between them that neither had to spell out in words.
quests.correctAnswer: There was an implicit agreement between them that neither had to spell out in words.

quests.hint: Stated clearly and directly, leaving no room for doubt.
quests.explanation: 'Explicit clauses' in a contract spell out exactly what happens. Its opposite is 'implicit,' understood without being said.
quests.textToSpeak: The contract contained very ___ clauses about what would happen in case of late delivery.
quests.correctAnswer: The contract contained very explicit clauses about what would happen in case of late delivery.

quests.hint: An earlier case or decision used as a model for similar situations later.
quests.explanation: 'Set a precedent' is the phrase to remember. 'Unprecedented' (the opposite) describes something with no earlier example to compare it to.
quests.textToSpeak: The court's ruling set an important ___ for how similar cases should be handled.
quests.correctAnswer: The court's ruling set an important precedent for how similar cases should be handled.

quests.hint: Gradually weakening something, often without a direct, open attack.
quests.explanation: 'Undermine confidence' or 'undermine authority' are worth learning together. It suggests damage happening slowly, from underneath.
quests.textToSpeak: His constant criticism of her work began to seriously ___ her self-confidence.
quests.correctAnswer: His constant criticism of her work began to seriously undermine her self-confidence.

quests.hint: The feeling or association a word carries, beyond its literal dictionary meaning.
quests.explanation: 'A positive connotation' or 'a negative connotation' describe the emotional shading of a word choice, different from its literal meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: The word 'slim' has a positive ___ while 'thin' can sometimes sound negative or unhealthy.
quests.correctAnswer: The word 'slim' has a positive connotation while 'thin' can sometimes sound negative or unhealthy.

quests.hint: A figure of speech describing one thing by directly calling it something else.
quests.explanation: 'Use a metaphor' is how most speakers say it. Unlike a simile, a metaphor doesn't use 'like' or 'as' — it states the comparison directly.
quests.textToSpeak: She used the ___ of a marathon to describe the long and tiring journey to recovery.
quests.correctAnswer: She used the metaphor of a marathon to describe the long and tiring journey to recovery.

quests.hint: Placing two very different things side by side to highlight the contrast between them.
quests.explanation: 'A striking juxtaposition' is a common phrase in film and art criticism. The verb form is 'juxtapose.'
quests.textToSpeak: The documentary creates a striking ___ between extreme wealth and grinding poverty.
quests.correctAnswer: The documentary creates a striking juxtaposition between extreme wealth and grinding poverty.

quests.hint: An indirect reference to another well-known work, person, or event.
quests.explanation: 'A clear allusion to' something is the natural choice here. Don't confuse it with 'illusion,' which means a false impression.
quests.textToSpeak: The poem contains a clear ___ to Milton's Paradise Lost in its final stanza.
quests.correctAnswer: The poem contains a clear allusion to Milton's Paradise Lost in its final stanza.

quests.hint: Using humour or exaggeration to criticise something, often politics or society.
quests.explanation: 'A sharp satire of' something is a common phrase. 'Satirical' is the adjective form.
quests.textToSpeak: The novel is a sharp ___ of the political system that made many people uncomfortable.
quests.correctAnswer: The novel is a sharp satire of the political system that made many people uncomfortable.

quests.hint: Saying something while clearly meaning the opposite, often for humorous effect.
quests.explanation: 'With clear irony' shows the speaker didn't mean it literally. 'Ironic' is the adjective form.
quests.textToSpeak: She said 'what a lovely day' with clear ___, given the torrential rain outside.
quests.correctAnswer: She said 'what a lovely day' with clear irony, given the torrential rain outside.

quests.hint: Extremely clear and easy to understand, even when the topic is complicated.
quests.explanation: 'Remarkably lucid' is high praise for an explanation. Its opposite is 'murky' or 'confusing.'
quests.textToSpeak: Despite the complexity of the topic, his lecture was remarkably ___ and easy to follow.
quests.correctAnswer: Despite the complexity of the topic, his lecture was remarkably lucid and easy to follow.

quests.hint: Using an existing resource or advantage to achieve something bigger.
quests.explanation: 'Leverage your network' is common in professional advice. As a noun, leverage also means influence or power in a negotiation.
quests.textToSpeak: She knew how to ___ her network to secure the funding needed for the project.
quests.correctAnswer: She knew how to leverage her network to secure the funding needed for the project.

quests.hint: Real and valuable, but impossible to physically touch or precisely measure.
quests.explanation: 'Intangible benefits' are the opposite of 'tangible' ones — things you can't put a number on, like trust or loyalty.
quests.textToSpeak: Trust and loyalty are ___ benefits of good leadership that cannot easily be measured.
quests.correctAnswer: Trust and loyalty are intangible benefits of good leadership that cannot easily be measured.

quests.hint: Real, concrete, and clearly measurable — the opposite of vague or abstract.
quests.explanation: 'Tangible results' are things you can actually point to and show. Its opposite is 'intangible.'
quests.textToSpeak: After six months of work, they finally had ___ results to show the investors.
quests.correctAnswer: After six months of work, they finally had tangible results to show the investors.

quests.hint: So important that everything else depends or turns on it.
quests.explanation: 'A pivotal moment' is a common phrase for a turning point. It comes from 'pivot,' the point something else rotates around.
quests.textToSpeak: That meeting turned out to be a truly ___ moment in the history of the organisation.
quests.correctAnswer: That meeting turned out to be a truly pivotal moment in the history of the organisation.

quests.hint: Never having happened before, with nothing similar to compare it to.
quests.explanation: 'Truly unprecedented' is a strong phrase for something genuinely new. Its opposite is 'precedent,' an earlier example to follow.
quests.textToSpeak: The scale of the challenge was truly ___ - nothing like this had ever occurred before.
quests.correctAnswer: The scale of the challenge was truly unprecedented - nothing like this had ever occurred before.

quests.hint: So influential that it shaped everything that came after it in a field.
quests.explanation: 'A seminal text' or 'a seminal work' describe something that started an entirely new direction of thinking.
quests.textToSpeak: Darwin's On the Origin of Species is considered the most ___ scientific text of its era.
quests.correctAnswer: Darwin's On the Origin of Species is considered the most seminal scientific text of its era.

quests.hint: A statement that seems contradictory but may actually be true.
quests.explanation: 'Something of a paradox' softens the claim slightly. 'Paradoxical' is the adjective form.
quests.textToSpeak: It is something of a ___ that working fewer hours can sometimes increase overall output.
quests.correctAnswer: It is something of a paradox that working fewer hours can sometimes increase overall output.

quests.hint: Finding a way to make two seemingly conflicting things fit together.
quests.explanation: 'Reconcile statements with actions' is the version people actually use. It can also mean two people making up after an argument.
quests.textToSpeak: It is hard to ___ her public statements with her private actions on the matter.
quests.correctAnswer: It is hard to reconcile her public statements with her private actions on the matter.

quests.hint: Existing as a natural, built-in part of something, not added from outside.
quests.explanation: 'An inherent tension' describes conflict built into the very nature of a situation. 'Inherently' is the adverb form.
quests.textToSpeak: There is an ___ tension between speed and quality that all designers must navigate.
quests.correctAnswer: There is an inherent tension between speed and quality that all designers must navigate.
